label: Merge
why: Superchunk's label. Home to Fust, Friendship, Hiss Golden Messenger (from 2014) and many Carolina acts.

label: Dear Life Records
why: Small label tied to the Wednesday and Lenderman circle; also Florry, Thomas Dollbaum, Natalie Jane Hill and Fust.

label: ANTI-
why: Released Manning Fireworks, Waxahatchee's recent records and Snocaps.

label: Paradise of Bachelors
why: Twangy folk and cosmic country. Hiss Golden Messenger's Poor Moon launched it; later Nap Eyes, Promised Land Sound, Mega Bog.

label: Sophomore Lounge
why: Ryan Davis's label: State Champion, Styrofoam Winos, Grace Rogers and Arbor Labor Union's later records.

label: Curation Records
why: Dead-indebted guitar rock and jangle: Silver Synthetic, Sean Thompson's Weird Ears, Sunday Mourners, GospelbeacH, Beachwood Sparks.

label: Keeled Scales
why: Soft Texas indie and folk: Lomelda, Will Johnson's later records, twain, Why Bonnie, Renée Reed.

label: Exploding in Sound
why: The best archive of noisy slacker rock (Speedy Ortiz, Pile, Ovlov).

label: Fire Talk
why: Adventurous indie rock, including Burlington's Robber Robber, Bnny and Wild Pink's Still Coming Down.

label: Lame-O Records
why: Philly's DIY indie and power pop: Hurry, 2nd Grade, Golden Apples, Lily Seabird, Saintseneca.

label: Drag City
why: Silver Jews, Palace, Smog and early Pavement. The home of the deadpan lyrical tradition; later Purple Mountains and Cory Hanson.

label: Bloodshot
why: The '90s insurgent country label: Waco Brothers, Robbie Fulks, Neko Case, Ryan Adams, Lydia Loveless, Justin Townes Earle.

label: SST
why: '80s punk label for Minutemen, Hüsker Dü, Meat Puppets and Dinosaur Jr. The backbone of the punk-to-college-rock network.

label: Twin/Tone
why: Early home of The Replacements; also Soul Asylum and the US Mekons.

label: Flying Nun
why: The roots of jangly slacker rock: The Clean, The Chills, The Verlaines, The Bats.

label: Matador
why: Pavement, Guided by Voices, Liz Phair, Yo La Tengo, Kurt Vile, Horsegirl: the slacker line from 1990 to now.

label: Sub Pop
why: Grunge first, then Iron & Wine, Fleet Foxes, Band of Horses, Arbor Labor Union, Scud Mountain Boys.

label: Secretly Canadian
why: Songs: Ohia and Magnolia Electric Co.; the label behind the Molina circle.

label: Jagjaguwar
why: Bon Iver, Angel Olsen and Okkervil River.

label: Dead Oceans
why: Phosphorescent, Bright Eyes' later records and Kevin Morby.

label: Saddle Creek
why: Bright Eyes, Cursive, Big Thief's first two albums and Hop Along.

label: 4AD
why: Big Thief from U.F.O.F. onward; earlier Tarnation and the Pixies.

label: Thrill Jockey
why: Arbouretum, Howe Gelb and a post-rock roster beside the V.

label: Woodsist
why: Jeremy Earl's label: Woods, early Real Estate, Kurt Vile, White Fence.

label: Run for Cover
why: Horse Jumper of Love and the twangier end of emo and indie rock.

label: Orindal Records
why: Hushed songwriters: Friendship, Advance Base, Dan Wriggins, Little Kid, Karima Walker.

label: Ruination Record Co.
why: Small folk and cosmic label: Erin Durant, Adeline Hotel, Frank Meadows.

label: No Quarter
why: Joan Shelley, Jana Horn and the Louisville folk circle.

label: New West
why: Later Old 97's, Corb Lund, Daniel Romano, The Deslondes, Esther Rose and Emily Nenni.

label: Yep Roc
why: Wednesday's early records, Trailer Bride, Jobi Riccio and much Americana.

label: Lost Highway
why: Ryan Adams, Lucinda Williams and the 2000s alt-country major-label boom.

label: Last Chance Records
why: Southern storytelling network: American Aquarium, Two Cow Garage, Glossary, John Moreland, Adam Faucett.

label: Loose Music
why: UK home for Americana; Brown Horse's label.

label: Takoma
why: John Fahey's label: the birth of American Primitive guitar (Fahey, Basho, Kottke).

label: Capricorn
why: The Allman Brothers Band and the Southern rock boom.

label: Slash
why: X, The Blasters, The Gun Club-era LA punk and roots rock.

label: La Honda Records
why: Colter Wall, Vincent Neil Emerson and Riddy Arman.

label: Oh Boy Records
why: John Prine's own label; now Kelsey Waldon, Arlo McKinley and Tre Burt.
